verdict.summary: Self-serve: create the OAuth app in GitHub settings and it works immediately. No review, no waiting.

questions.text: Will your users connect accounts that belong to GitHub organizations?

variants.summary: Your app works immediately, but each customer organization may have to approve it before members can grant access to org repositories.
variants.calendar_label: Same day for you; depends on each org owner
notes: New organizations restrict OAuth apps by default.
Consider a GitHub App instead: GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies.

byo_advice: Composio has a managed GitHub app, so you can start without creating your own. Bring your own when you want your product name on the consent screen, your own rate limits, or scopes beyond Composio's defaults.

before_you_start.text: A GitHub account (sign in with password, Google, Apple or a passkey). The new-app page redirects straight to sign-in; there is no developer program to join.

evidence.label: TESTED
evidence.note: github.com/settings/applications/new redirected to github.com/login on 2026-10-21; the page offered password, Google, Apple and passkey sign-in.

before_you_start.text: Only use information you are happy to make public in the app's fields.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.detail: Open https://github.com/settings/applications/new. You'll be sent to GitHub sign-in first.

evidence.label: TESTED
evidence.note: Observed redirect to github.com/login with return_to set.

steps.title: Open Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App
steps.detail: Profile picture > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App (reads 'Register a new application' if you have none). The URL above opens it directly.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings

steps.title: Fill in name, homepage and description
steps.detail: Use your product name and public homepage. The description is optional and shown to users.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public

steps.title: Set the Authorization callback URL to Composio's callback
steps.detail: Paste the redirect URI from your Composio auth config.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app

steps.title: Leave 'Expire user access tokens' on
steps.detail: It's on by default. Composio refreshes tokens for you.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default

steps.title: Click Register application
steps.detail: The app works immediately; there is no review.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: That no review follows comes from our research and the absence of any review step in GitHub's docs; not observed in a signed-in run.

steps.title: Generate a client secret and add both values to Composio
steps.detail: Generate a client secret on the app page, then create a Composio auth config for GitHub with the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: set its authorized redirect URI to Composio's callback, then pass the client ID and secret
evidence.note: Where to generate the secret on GitHub was not visible without signing in.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: No review process appears in GitHub's OAuth app docs; GitHub Marketplace listing (optional) is separate.

customer_gates.text: New GitHub organizations restrict OAuth apps by default, so an org owner may need to approve your app before members can grant it access to org resources.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default

gotchas.text: If org approvals are a problem for your users, a GitHub App avoids them.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies

gotchas.text: New OAuth apps issue expiring user tokens by default, so your integration must handle refresh (Composio does).

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default

blockers.symptom: Users in an organization can connect, but the agent can't see that org's repositories.
blockers.cause: The organization restricts OAuth apps and hasn't approved yours.
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to approve the app under the org's third-party access settings, or switch to a GitHub App.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources

blockers.symptom: The connect flow fails with a redirect URI mismatch error.
blockers.cause: The Authorization callback URL doesn't exactly match the redirect URI in your Composio auth config.
blockers.fix: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio auth config into the GitHub app's callback URL field, character for character.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Exact GitHub error wording not verified in this run.

scopes.why: Only if your agent must read or write private repositories; it grants broad access, so omit it if public data is enough.
